title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measures the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded minus baseline), implemented as paired success-rate difference per the preregistration. Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable misconfigurations under original power assumptions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed in the preregistered power calculation. We reconcile estimand algebra, expand execution/accounting and reproducibility details, and point auditors to archived artifact paths and SHA-256 digests for forensic verification.

sections.introduction: LLM-based intent→configuration systems promise rapid NetOps productivity gains but raise operational risk when generated configurations are syntactically correct yet semantically or policy-wise unsafe. A common mitigation is to interpose deterministic validators and automated repair loops (generate→verify→repair, GVR). Despite frequent system proposals, the marginal operational benefit of a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract (single hosted LLM, limited automated repairs) is not well quantified with preregistered confirmatory methods and full forensic artifact traceability. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our contributions are: (1) a fully preregistered paired confirmatory run with complete artifact hashing and deterministic validator traces; (2) exact, artifact-grounded paired analysis results and algebraic reconciliation between success-rate and actionable-error estimands; and (3) reproducibility accounting (provider-call audit, per-episode validator traces, and manifest SHA-256 digests) enabling forensic re-computation of all reported statistics.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification (header-space analysis, incremental checkers, VeriFlow) provides pre-deployment safety foundations. Recent LLM→NetOps efforts evaluate intent-driven generation (NetConfEval, LLM-enabled intent configuration) but often omit preregistration, shared-initial candidate designs, bounded repair contracts, or forensic hashing of provider calls and validator traces. Our work differs by (i) using a shared_initial generation to produce identical LLM candidates for baseline and guarded arms, (ii) enforcing a strict adapter contract (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1), (iii) applying a deterministic validator that emits canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks, and (iv) publishing cryptographic digests for all principal artifacts to permit exact re-derivation of contingency tables and per-episode traces.
sections.methodology:
Design and preregistration. The paired binary design (N=200 tasks) and analysis plan were preregistered (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001; preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815ea...). The primary_estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = not actionable-error). The preregistered confirmatory test is exact McNemar two-sided; a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was also prespecified. Planned stratification (preregistered) was Cisco-like N=66, Juniper-like N=67, RFC-neutral N=67; these planned counts appear in the preregistration artifacts and are repeated in Table 4.

Adapter contract, model, and generation semantics. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and declared_model_version/requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e2...). The adapter enforced shared_initial generation semantics (one initial candidate reused across baseline and guarded conditions) and permitted at most one automated repair call per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Provider-call accounting is recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...), which reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}. The execution manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) records planned_episode_count = 400 and completed_episode_count = 400.

Synthetic task bank and deterministic validator. The deterministic multi-vendor synthetic task bank was produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies (must_be_down_for_fields, make_before_break, etc.), allowed touched fields, and an explicit required_sequence. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses LLM responses into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax and semantic/workflow policies, and runs simulator-backed intent-constraint checks to produce validator_trace objects (validation_before, validation_after) and a binary score per scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Per-episode scoring JSONs are archived under execution/scoring/ (representative examples and SHA-256 digests are included in the evidence bundle).

Execution, retries, and missingness. The preregistered missingness plan attempted up to two automatic retries on provider-call failures and would exclude irrecoverable technical failures from the primary paired analysis. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution manifest: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200. All provider calls and stage counts are logged and hashed; execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e2... and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8... are authoritative.

Analysis procedures. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 consumed execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) and produced contingency counts (n_11,n_10,n_01,n_00), an exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000). The archive contains analysis CSVs and logs (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba..., analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56..., analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b...). Multiplicity control: single preregistered primary hypothesis; secondary/exploratory tests explicitly labeled exploratory in the preregistration.
sections.results:
Primary paired outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200; baseline_success_count = 199 (0.995); guarded_success_count = 200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba...) reports: n_11 = 199 (guarded=1 & baseline=1), n_10 = 1 (guarded=1 & baseline=0), n_01 = 0 (guarded=0 & baseline=1), n_00 = 0 (both invalid). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI for the absolute paired difference = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729).

Estimand algebra and hypothesis reconciliation. The preregistration described H1 as a ≥50% relative reduction in actionable-error rate; the analysis executor implements the primary_estimand as guarded_success − baseline_success. Because actionable_error_rate = 1 − success_rate, a 50% relative reduction in actionable-error rate maps to a small absolute difference when baseline actionable-error prevalence is tiny. Observed baseline actionable-error rate = 1 − 0.995 = 0.005 (1/200). A 50% relative reduction of that baseline corresponds to absolute change 0.0025, i.e., guarded_success − baseline_success = +0.0025 in success-rate terms. Our observed absolute paired change = +0.005 exceeds that mapped absolute value, but the preregistered power calculation was sized for much larger absolute effects (target absolute reduction ≈ 0.15). Thus the preregistered confirmatory design lacked power to regard small absolute improvements in the rare-failure regime as confirmatory evidence for the originally framed large-effect hypothesis. We therefore report the exact artifact-grounded contingency counts, CI, and p-value, and explain algebraically why the preregistered power assumptions are inconsistent with the observed rare-failure regime.

Provider-call accounting and repair activity. Provider-call audit (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_miss_count = 201, and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}. This explains model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair) as recorded in the execution manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). The single repair-stage invocation corresponds to the one discordant improvement recorded in n_10 = 1.

Per‑vendor stratification and reviewer requests. The preregistered planned strata were Cisco-like N=66, Juniper-like N=67, RFC-neutral N=67 (Table 4 and preregistration artifacts). Observed per-vendor stratified counts are computable deterministically from execution/task_manifest.jsonl and the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/; the authoritative artifacts are execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e...) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). Because the supplied manuscript evidence bundle does not include a verbatim printed table of the observed per-vendor counts, we provide the artifact pointers and SHA-256 digests so auditors can derive and verify those numbers exactly (see Disclosure Statement and reproducibility section).
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained test regime (synthetic 200-task bank, single model gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator v5, single automated repair), the guarded pipeline yielded a numerically small absolute improvement because the baseline generator already produced extremely few actionable errors (1/200). In operational terms, the marginal value of a deterministic validator depends on baseline LLM error prevalence, validator semantic coverage, repair budget, human review cost, and risk tolerance. When baseline error prevalence is already low, additional validator investment yields small absolute risk reductions; system designers should align validation effort with expected baseline error mass and cost of residual failures.

Post-hoc power and sensitivity interpretation. The preregistered power plan targeted a detectable absolute reduction ≈0.15 and assumed a substantially higher baseline actionable-error rate. Using the observed baseline error rate (0.005), the study's detectable absolute differences shrink and the original power calibration becomes inappropriate. We compute (artifact-grounded) that, with baseline error = 0.005 and N=200, detecting a 50% relative reduction (absolute 0.0025) would require dramatically larger N; auditors can recompute sensitivity curves from archived execution counts (execution/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56...). This is a practical lesson for future confirmatory runs: either increase N, oversample high-difficulty tasks, or use cost-weighted estimands for rare failure regimes.

Failure-mode diagnostics. The single discordant improvement (n_10 = 1) is an explicit per-episode record in the raw results and per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/; the execution manifest and analysis artifacts list the hashes where the full validator_trace and provider-call trace for that episode are stored (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8..., execution/scoring/ files hashed in the full manifest). We do not print the episode id verbatim in this text because the supplied manuscript evidence bundle does not include that identifier verbatim; auditors can extract the identifier deterministically using the provided SHA-256 keyed artifacts. The contamination summary (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA-256 = 389227f0...) shows no systematic contamination clusters; the single baseline failure was a simple syntactic/ordering omission that the single repair invocation corrected.

Threats to validity and limitations (summary). Internal validity: prompt and adapter sensitivity, single repair budget, and shared_initial semantics may alter generality. Construct validity: synthetic task bank and deterministic validator coverage bound how closely the scoring maps to production risk. External validity: single-model evidence (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic tasks limit generalization to other models and live networks. Conclusion validity: rare-event baseline (1/200) yields low discordant-pair mass and imprecise inference for small absolute effects. We enumerate additional limitations in the Disclosure Statement and the manuscript limitations list.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered confirmatory paired experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a bounded adapter contract. On the synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect hypothesis (sized for absolute changes ≈0.15) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence was substantially lower than assumed, illustrating the importance of aligning power planning with expected rare-event regimes. All principal artifacts, provider-call accounting, validator traces, and analysis CSVs are archived and SHA-256 hashed to permit forensic reproduction of every reported contingency cell, CI, and p-value. Future work should broaden model diversity, increase task realism and difficulty oversampling, expand repair budgets, and evaluate multiple deterministic validators to identify settings where guarded GVR pipelines produce materially large operational risk reductions.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Reviewer-required per-vendor stratified observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are not included verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle; auditors can compute them from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) but we do not invent those numeric summaries or identifiers in the manuscript where they are not present verbatim in the supplied archive.
